title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: OBM Person
tiers.description: Each director, employee and contractor of the Company Group. Bound (and must procure that Connected Persons are bound) by the insider trading rule, the no-speculative-trading rule, the no-protection-arrangements rule and the no-security/margin-lending rule.

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: Each member of Key Management Personnel and any other person designated as a Restricted Person by the Managing Director in writing. Subject, in addition to the OBM Person rules, to prior written approval before any Dealing in OBM Shares and to the Blackout Periods.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Has the meaning given in the Corporations Act; automatically Restricted Persons, and additionally must notify the Company Secretary of every Dealing (including exempt Dealings) for ASIC/ASX reporting purposes.

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: In relation to an OBM Person: a spouse (including de facto); a child under 18 (including step- or adopted child); any other person over whose trading or investment decisions the OBM Person has control or influence; and a company or trust controlled by the OBM Person or any of the foregoing.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any OBM Person's (or any of their Connected Persons') security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements)

windows.start_anchor: close of the ASX trading day on 31 December
windows.end_anchor: 10:00am AEDT on the ASX trading day following release of the Company's half yearly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Managing Director may specify any other Blackout Period from time to time (3.3(d)). Confidentiality of such a period is not directly addressed, though a refusal of approval to deal must be kept confidential (5.2(c)).

rules.detail: 'Protection arrangements' expressly include OBM products in the derivatives markets; over unvested OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities this is banned at any time with no approval route, for all OBM Persons and their Connected Persons.
rules.evidence: OBM Persons must not, and must procure that their Connected Persons do not, enter into any type of "protection arrangements" for any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities (or OBM products in the derivatives markets): (a) in respect of any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock – at any time.

rules.detail: The absolute ban on protection arrangements expressly extends to securities 'subject to a holding lock', with no approval route.
rules.evidence: in respect of any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock – at any time

rules.detail: Over vested, non-locked holdings, a protection arrangement (including an OTC derivative operating to limit economic risk) is permitted with prior written approval from the Authorising Officer.
rules.evidence: otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements are given as the express example of an arrangement that 'operates to limit the economic risk' of a holding; banned at any time over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any OBM Person's (or any of their Connected Persons') security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including where the OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities are held beneficially ... on their ... behalf

rules.detail: Same absolute ban applies to holding-locked vested securities.
rules.evidence: in respect of any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock – at any time

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unrestricted holdings is permitted with prior written approval; even a beneficial holding through a trust or Incentive Plan is covered.
rules.evidence: otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a structure that operates to limit the economic risk of the holding is a protection arrangement, banned at any time over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any OBM Person's ... security holding

rules.detail: A monetisation structure over vested, unrestricted holdings is caught as a protection arrangement and is permitted with prior approval.
rules.evidence: otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.

rules.detail: Short selling beyond the person's (or Connected Person's) holding is expressly named as a protection arrangement; banned at any time over unvested securities (there is little practical scope to short sell an unvested holding, but the clause is drafted without that limitation).
rules.evidence: amount to "short selling" of securities beyond the OBM Person's (or any of their Connected Persons') holding of securities

rules.detail: Short selling beyond holding is permitted, subject to prior approval, once the underlying holding is vested and unrestricted.
rules.evidence: otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. It might be a 'disposal' under the Dealing definition (transfer of legal title) but this is not addressed expressly.
A CFD used on a short-term or speculative basis is expressly named and banned outright, with no clearance route, regardless of vesting state.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct Dealing in OBM Shares as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Even a non-speculative CFD over unvested securities would be a protection arrangement (limiting economic risk / short selling beyond holding) and is banned at any time.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any OBM Person's ... security holding

rules.detail: A non-speculative CFD over vested, unrestricted holdings is a protection arrangement requiring prior approval, provided it is not short-term or speculative (which would be an outright ban under 3.4).
rules.evidence: otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.

rules.detail: Entering a margin lending arrangement involving unvested or holding-locked OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities is banned at any time, no approval route.
rules.evidence: OBM Persons may not, and must procure that their Connected Persons do not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities.

rules.detail: Same absolute ban applies to holding-locked vested securities.
rules.evidence: over any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Margin lending over vested, unrestricted holdings is permitted (subject to any applicable Company Incentive Plan rules) with prior written approval.
rules.evidence: OBM Persons and their Connected Persons may, if they obtain approval under section 5.1, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security (charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over unvested or holding-locked securities, to secure any obligation of that person or a third party, is banned at any time.
rules.evidence: OBM Persons may not ... grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that person or any third party.

rules.detail: Granting security over vested, unrestricted holdings to secure the person's own or a third party's obligation is permitted with prior approval.
rules.evidence: Unless sub-section (a) applies ... OBM Persons and their Connected Persons may, if they obtain approval under section 5.1, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... to secure any obligation of that person or any third party.

rules.detail: Any secured financing (security granted over the shares to secure an obligation of the person or a third party, or a margin lending arrangement) is banned at any time for unvested or holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: to secure any obligation of that person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities

rules.detail: Not prohibited outright: a bank loan secured on vested, unrestricted OBM Shares (to secure the OBM Person's own obligation) is permitted subject to prior written approval from the Authorising Officer.
rules.evidence: OBM Persons and their Connected Persons may, if they obtain approval under section 5.1, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... to secure any obligation of that person or any third party.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading (direct or via derivatives); no period is defined and no clearance route is given for this specific rule.
rules.evidence: OBM Persons must not, and must procure that their Connected Persons do not, engage in short-term or speculative trading in OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities.

clearance.approver: Authorising Officer: chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (for the Chair of the Board); chair of the Board or, in their absence, chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (for the Managing Director); Managing Director or, in their absence, chair of the Board (for any other person)
clearance.evidence: Before a Restricted Person (or any of their Connected Persons) Deals in OBM Shares they must: notify the relevant person ... obtain the written approval from the Authorising Officer, which approval may be given or refused ... without the need to give any reasons. ... Any written approval granted under this Policy will be valid for the period of 5 trading days from the time which it is given ... Written approval ... may be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer in writing, in person or by email at any time during the approval period.

clearance.approver: Authorising Officer (same table as for Restricted Persons)
clearance.evidence: Before an OBM Person does any other thing requiring them to obtain approval under this Policy they must: notify the relevant Authorising Officer of the proposed activity; and obtain the written approval from the Authorising Officer.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately, and no later than 2 business days after the event
clearance.evidence: a member of Key Management Personnel must immediately (and no later than two business days after any relevant event) notify the Company Secretary in writing of the occurrence of any Dealing (including any exempt Dealing under this Policy).

short_term.evidence: OBM Persons must not, and must procure that their Connected Persons do not, engage in short-term or speculative trading in OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities.

exceptions.evidence: applying for Incentive Plan Securities; being issued or otherwise acquiring Incentive Plan Securities; the vesting of Incentive Plan Securities; the exercise or conversion of Incentive Plan Securities into OBM Shares ... are not regulated by this Policy and may be undertaken by an OBM Person or their Connected Persons at any time.
Trading in OBM Shares where the trading does not result in any change of beneficial interest in the OBM Shares.

Transferring OBM Shares already held ... into a self-managed superannuation fund, family trust, private company or other saving scheme in which the OBM Person or their Connected Person (as applicable) is a beneficiary or shareholder and which the OBM Person or any of their Connected Persons controls.
Acquiring OBM Shares under a bonus issue, dividend or capital reduction made to all holders of securities of the same class.
Undertaking to accept, or accepting, a takeover offer.
Disposing of OBM Shares under a scheme of arrangement under Part 5.1 of the Corporations Act.

Investing in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in OBM Shares) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

A disposal of OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement, subject to the grant of security having been granted with approval under section 5.1.

Where an OBM Person or any of their Connected Persons is a trustee, trading in the securities managed by that trust provided the OBM Person or their Connected Person ... is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently.

Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the Company's security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back, where the plan ... has been approved by the Board.

In exceptional circumstances an Authorising Officer has discretion to approve under section 5.1: (a) Dealings in OBM Shares during a Blackout Period; or (b) other Dealings, that would otherwise be prohibited by this Policy but are not prohibited by law ... may include ... severe financial hardship.
may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship or a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking.

financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel: any Dealing including exempt Dealings (e.g. a secured lender's forced sale), to the Company Secretary, immediately and no later than 2 business days after the event, for ASIC/ASX notification purposes.

exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer has absolute, case-by-case discretion under 4.3 to approve Dealings during a Blackout Period, or other Dealings otherwise prohibited by the Policy but not prohibited by law, for severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking. Whether this discretion can extend to override the separate 'at any time' bans on protection arrangements and security-granting/margin lending over unvested or holding-locked securities (3.5(a), 3.6(a)) is untested, since those bans are not framed as prohibitions on 'Dealing' (the defined term used in 4.3).

bespoke_clauses.clause: OBM Persons must not ... enter into any type of "protection arrangements" ... (a) in respect of any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock – at any time; and (b) otherwise – without approval under section 5.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition on hedging/protection arrangements (and the parallel prohibition on granting security/margin lending in 3.6) is tied to vesting status, not to tier: it is an absolute, clearance-free bar while shares are unvested or subject to a holding lock, but becomes merely approval-gated once the shares vest and any holding lock lifts. A funded collar is therefore only conceivable over shares that have fully vested and are no longer holding-locked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement, subject to the grant of security having been granted with approval under section 5.1 [is not regulated by this Policy and may be undertaken ... at any time].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, OBM expressly exempts a bank's enforcement sale on default from the Policy altogether, including during a Blackout Period, so long as the original grant of security over the shares was itself approved. This directly de-risks the lender's ability to enforce the collar loan's security without the borrower being put in breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any OBM Shares or Incentive Plan Securities ... to secure any obligation of that person or any third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The security-granting prohibition/approval regime is not limited to bank margin loans; it expressly covers any charge, mortgage or pledge securing any obligation (even a third party's), so the collar loan's security interest is squarely within scope and needs 5.1 approval once shares are vested and unrestricted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written approval granted under this Policy will be valid for the period of 5 trading days ... Written approval ... may be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer in writing, in person or by email at any time during the approval period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar (derivative legs and/or security grant) must be executed within 5 trading days, and the Authorising Officer can revoke the approval at any point before execution, so timing and re-clearance risk should be built into the transaction schedule.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances an Authorising Officer has discretion to approve under section 5.1: (a) Dealings in OBM Shares during a Blackout Period; or (b) other Dealings, that would otherwise be prohibited by this Policy but are not prohibited by law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is unclear whether this hardship/court-order override (framed around 'Dealings') can reach the separately-worded absolute bans on protection arrangements and security-granting over unvested/holding-locked shares, since those bans are not expressed as prohibitions on 'Dealing'; the bank should not assume this route can unlock a collar before full vesting.

summary: A funded collar is workable under this policy, but only once the underlying OBM shares have fully vested and any holding lock has lifted: over unvested or holding-locked shares, both the derivative legs (a 'protection arrangement' under 3.5, expressly including hedging and short selling) and the loan's security (3.6) are banned at any time with no exception. Once the shares are vested and unrestricted, both legs become merely approval-gated: an OBM Person or their Connected Person may enter into the protection arrangement and grant security over the shares (to secure their own or even a third party's obligation, covering the bank loan) with prior written approval from the Authorising Officer (5 trading days' validity, revocable, refusal confidential but not final in the sense that a fresh request can always be made). Execution must also avoid the quarterly, half-year and full-year Blackout Periods (and any additional period set by the Board or Managing Director) unless the Authorising Officer grants an exceptional-circumstances approval for hardship or a court order. Distinctively, OBM's policy expressly carves out a secured lender's enforcement sale on default from the Policy altogether, including during a Blackout Period, provided the original security grant was itself approved, which meaningfully de-risks the bank's enforcement rights. Key Management Personnel must separately notify the Company Secretary of every Dealing, including exempt ones, within two business days for ASIC/ASX reporting.
